title: Dealing with Breakdowns in Communication - Interpersonal and Intergroup
coreMove: Respond to a breakdown by first understanding the other side's frame strongly enough that defense can drop.
sourcePressure: The chapter applies Rogers' relational logic to communication breakdowns between individuals and groups. No split source sidecar exists for ch17; frozen TOC and book skeleton support the heading, part placement, and broad intent only, with no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing intergroup communication to civility, politeness, or better messaging.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.
